records.people: Ibrahim Mohammed Ali Nimir (General Manager, Central Bank of Sudan, 1964-1967; Governor and Chairman of the Board of Directors, 1973-1980)
records.move: from General Manager of the Central Bank of Sudan (1964-1967) to General Manager of Elneilin Bank (1970-1973), then back to the central bank as Governor and Board Chairman (1973-1980)
records.summary: The Central Bank of Sudan's own page on its former governors lists Nimir's posts in order: General Manager of the central bank 1964-1967, General Manager of Elneilin Bank 1970-1973, then Governor and Chairman of the Board 1973-1980. The bank's page states no ownership for Elneilin Bank. El Nilein Bank's own group history page settles it the other way: it says the bank, formed in 1963 from a merger of Credit Lyonnais, the Arab Bank and the Red Sea Bank, was 'Nationalized and became El Nilein Bank Group' in 1970 and only 'became an independent entity' in 2007. Nimir's 1970-1973 term therefore began in the year the bank passed into state hands, which makes this leg a public-sector move, not a move into private finance.
records.source_title: Former Governors - Ibrahim Mohammed Ali Nimir (Central Bank of Sudan)
records.second_source_quote: Nationalized and became El Nilein Bank Group

records.people: Ibrahim Mohammed Ali Nimir (Governor and Chairman of the Board of Directors, Central Bank of Sudan, 1973-1980)
records.move: from Governor and Board Chairman of the Central Bank of Sudan (1973-1980) to General Manager of National Bank (1980-1982) and later General Manager of Workers National Bank (1989-1992)
records.summary: The same Central Bank of Sudan page lists, after his governorship, 'General Manager, National Bank, 1980 - 1982' and 'General Manager, Workers National Bank, 1989 - 1992'. Neither employer's ownership is stated on that page, and nothing found this round states who owned either bank in those years; Sudan nationalised its banks in 1970 and reversed course in stages afterwards, so the years matter and these two legs are not settled either way.

records.people: Jeong Gyu-il (Deputy Governor, Bank of Korea; joined the bank in 1987)
records.move: from Deputy Governor of the Bank of Korea to chief executive and president of Seoul Foreign Exchange Brokerage (announced 2 July 2021)
records.summary: Asia Economic Daily reports that Seoul Foreign Exchange Brokerage appointed Jeong Gyu-il as its chief executive and president at an extraordinary shareholders' meeting; it says he joined the Bank of Korea in 1987 and held senior posts there - Deputy Director of the Economic Research Institute, Director of International Cooperation and Director of Economic Statistics - before becoming Deputy Governor, without giving dates for those roles. No source opened states who owns Seoul Foreign Exchange Brokerage: its own LEI record (as Seoul Money Brokerage Services, Ltd.) gives 'Parent Information Not Provided' for both direct and ultimate parent, and the appointment article names no shareholders. Ownership unsettled.

records.people: Stephen Mpuuga Kaboyo (senior executive positions, Bank of Uganda; no dates given)
records.move: from senior executive positions at the Bank of Uganda to founder and Managing Director of Alpha Capital Partners
records.summary: Uganda Reinsurance Company's profile page for Kaboyo states that he 'served at Bank of Uganda in Senior Executive positions' and that he is 'founder and Managing Director of Alpha Capital Partners'. It gives no dates for either, and it states no ownership for Alpha Capital Partners; that he founded the firm himself is the only thing the page says bearing on ownership, so ownership is not settled on the face of the record. Filed in place of the Blasio Kizza lead, which did not yield: a web search for 'Blasio Kizza' returned no biography of him at all, so the years of his Uganda Commercial Bank service remain unknown and that lead stays unsettled.

records.people: Jaime Valencia Valencia (General Manager, Banco Central de Bolivia, 1996-2006 and again from 16 January 2020)
records.move: from Banco de la Union S.A. to General Manager of the Banco Central de Bolivia (no dates given for the bank post)
records.summary: Valencia's CV on the Banco Central de Bolivia's own site names three financial employers with no titles and no dates: Banco de la Union S.A., Banco de Cochabamba S.A. and Compania Boliviana de Seguros S.A. The ownership of one of the three is now stated, and it points the other way: the English Wikipedia article on Banco Union says the Bolivian government 'established a new public financial entity called Banco de la Union S.A.' by public deed on 28 July 1979 and that 'Through the National Treasury, the government established a 97% stake in the new bank', describing it as a Bolivian state bank. On that statement the Banco de la Union leg is a public-sector move. Because the CV gives no dates, it cannot be excluded that he was there in a period of different ownership. The other two employers are still unsettled: ASFI's 1999 annual report lists 'Banco de Cochabamba S.A. en Liquidacion' under the heading 'ENTIDADES EN LIQUIDACION', which is a status and not an ownership statement, and nothing opened this round states the ownership of Compania Boliviana de Seguros S.A.

records.people: Abdel Aziz Ould Dahi (Governor, Banque Centrale de Mauritanie, from January 2015)
records.move: from Director General of the Caisse Nationale d'Assurance Maladie (CNAM) to Governor of the Banque Centrale de Mauritanie (January 2015)
records.summary: Financial Afrik reports Ould Dahi's appointment as governor and says that until then he was 'Directeur General de la Caisse Nationale d'Assurance Maladie (CNAM)', the national health insurance fund, and that he had been a minister under President Sidi Mohamed Ould Cheikh Abdallahi. CNAM is a statutory public insurance body, so this is a public-sector move. The article names no commercial bank, private bank, insurer or finance company in his career.

checked_none: Ibrahim Mohammed Ali Nimir (SDN): El Nilein Bank's own group history page settles Elneilin Bank's ownership against the row - 'Nationalized and became El Nilein Bank Group' in 1970, 'an independent entity' only in 2007, so his 1970-1973 term was at a state-owned bank. The Central Bank of Sudan's bank locator entry for EL NILEIN BANK gives only the classification field 'Commercial', with no ownership; the Zawya company profile puts ownership details behind a paid sign-up; the Sudan Transparency banking report and the Library of Congress country study (countrystudies.us) do not state ownership for Elneilin Bank, National Bank or Workers National Bank in the 1970s-1990s, the country study saying only that after the 1970 Nationalization of Banks Act 'all domestic banks have been controlled by the Bank of Sudan'.

Seoul Foreign Exchange Brokerage (KOR): its LEI record (as Seoul Money Brokerage Services, Ltd.) gives 'Parent Information Not Provided' for both direct and ultimate parent, reason NON_CONSOLIDATING; no ownership statement found. Needs a hand check of the firm's own site (smbs.biz), which no search returned, so it could not be opened under the provenance rule.

Blasio Kizza (UGA): a web search for his name returned no biography of him; no dated account of his Uganda Commercial Bank service found, so whether he was there before or after the 2002 sale to Stanbic is still unknown.

Aivo Andrianarivelo (MDG, Governor of Banky Foiben'i Madagasikara from 4 January 2023): the Africa Financial Industry Summit speaker bio says he worked '30 years as an economist in banking and finance' and 'gained previous experience at bank level' but names no bank; the employers it does name are Catholic Relief Services, the Fonds de Portage et de Privatisation ('a company that manages and sells shares on behalf of the Malagasy government'), the Ministry of Economy and Finance and the IMF - all public or non-financial.

Jean Baden Dubois and Charles Castel (HTI, Bank of the Republic of Haiti): the Central Banking report on Dubois's appointment names only his earlier BRH director-general post, and for Castel only BRH roles and public-sector work; no private financial employer.

Bonivert Claude (HTI, BRH Governor end of November 1991 to October 1994): his biography gives BNRH from January 1966, deputy director then director of economic studies from August 1979, board member February-December 1982 and June 1985-March 1986, then governor; no commercial or private bank. His non-bank venture EFCTEC (1974) is not financial employment.

Mohamed El Cheikh El Kebir Moulaye (MRT, Governor from 21 January 2020): Financial Afrik's profile names only BCM posts, the savings and credit network PROCAPEC, and two ministries - already on the map as a public move.
Cheikh Kebir Ould Moulaye Taher (MRT, deputy governor named January 2014): the appointment report gives no prior employer and no dates, and names no private financial firm.
Ahmed Osman Ali (DJI, Governor of the Banque Centrale de Djibouti): the Next Is Africa profile identifies him by title only and gives no career history at all.

CRDB Bank Burundi (BDI): its English top-management page carries no biographies and no ownership statement beyond a 2009 Dar es Salaam Stock Exchange listing; the leadership and group pages were not served.

Interbank Burundi (BDI): the 2024 annual report's board and executive-committee lists give names and titles only, no biographies, and the served part names no shareholder - only 'l'ensemble des actionnaires' and share capital of BIF 50,220,800 thousand.

Grupo Popular / Banco Popular Dominicano (DOM): the group's own board-of-directors biographies name neither the Banco Central de la Republica Dominicana nor the Junta Monetaria, and state no ownership.

Produbanco (ECU): its 2023 corporate report lists board and management names and roles without career histories; the Banco Central del Ecuador appears only as a statistical source. The report does describe Produbanco as 'el unico banco de capital privado en Latinoamerica', so its private ownership is stated - but no career is attached to it yet.

Alejandro Ribadeneira Jaramillo (ECU, general manager of Banco Pichincha): the Primicias profile gives 30 years in banking, 11 years as general manager of Banco General Ruminahui and Banco Pichincha finance vice-president since 2018 - no central bank and no public body, so not a revolving-door move.
dfcu (UGA): the page served carries no board or management biographies and no ownership statement.
Caroline Abel and the Central Bank of Seychelles (SYC): no page opened this round; search returned only encyclopaedia and interview pages, no career list naming a private financial employer.
